sources.evidence: Shift your electricity use to the daytime, when CPA generation rates are zero* , and use less electricity overnight and during evening peak hours when electricity is more expensive.

sources.evidence: I reviewed enough units to know the opportunity is there if the station has a time-of-use mode (TOU, for short).
You’ll be charged the highest rate for electricity used during peak times, and electricity will be the cheapest during off-peak times.

missing: A worked payback calculation: peak vs off-peak spread, usable kWh after round-trip losses, annual dollar savings, and cost per station. It should also list which stations have TOU mode, and say whether any beat the cost of the station.
why: Only one real answer exists, a Popular Mechanics piece that appears three times via syndication. It is qualitative and gives no savings math. The rest are generic utility TOU pages, a DOE microgrid page and a solar installer's article. No major reviewer gives tested savings figures or payback numbers, so a page with a calculator and rate-spread math would stand out.
